name: French Rolls (No. 2)
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: milk (new, warm milk is best)

ingredients.name: and a pint of flour

instructions.text: Make a sponge with milk, yeast, and flour

When this sponge is light, work in a well-beaten egg and two tablespoonfuls melted butter, with a teaspoonful of salt, half a teaspoonful soda dissolved in hot water, one tablespoonful white sugar and enough white flour to make a soft dough
Let this stand four or five hours
Roll out into round cakes and fold as in No. 1, or shape with your hands into balls
Set these closely together in the baking-pan
Just before putting them into the oven, cut deeply across each ball with a sharp knife

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Make a sponge with milk, yeast, and flour
2. When this sponge is light, work in a well-beaten egg and two tablespoonfuls melted butter, with a teaspoonful of salt, half a teaspoonful soda dissolved in hot water, one tablespoonful white sugar and enough white flour to make a soft dough
3. Let this stand four or five hours
4. Roll out into round cakes and fold as in No. 1, or shape with your hands into balls
5. Set these closely together in the baking-pan
6. Let them rise one hour
7. Just before putting them into the oven, cut deeply across each ball with a sharp knife
8. Bake half an hour
originalIngredients: 1 quart milk (new, warm milk is best)
1 quart and a pint of flour
half a teaspoonful soda dissolved in hot water
